_comment: Permission defaults for a claude-code-sdlc project.
WHY THESE EXIST: an unattended pipeline run that stalls on a permission
prompt has failed. The allow list covers the commands the pipeline needs
to run itself; the deny list is the fail-closed floor for actions that are
irreversible or that would let the agent widen its own permissions.
Edit(**) and Write(**) are anchored to the project root, and in-tree edits
are git-recoverable because the pipeline commits after every slice. They
are only safe alongside the settings-file, .git/** and secrets denies
below - without those, an agent could rewrite this very policy. Do not
remove a deny entry without removing the matching allow.
WHAT THIS CANNOT CATCH: these are prefix patterns, not a sandbox. Option
reordering (rm -r -f /), absolute binary paths (/bin/rm), indirection
through a script or variable, base64-packed payloads, and compound
commands can all evade them. More fundamentally, running a project's own
tests is arbitrary code execution by design - that is inside this
harness's trust boundary. This list protects against mistake
amplification and casual prompt-injected one-liners. It is a guardrail,
not a sandbox.
No 'ask' key: an ask entry is a guaranteed stall in an unattended run and
adds nothing over deny, which is fail-closed without stalling.
No 'hooks' key: plugin hooks auto-load, so duplicating them here makes
every hook fire twice.
Projects that genuinely need curl/wget can re-allow them in
.claude/settings.local.json, which is gitignored and personal.
statusLine below renders .claude/statusline.js in Claude Code's own
status bar (FR-13). It is not a hook and has no reverse dependency on
this pipeline - nothing here reads its output back in, so removing it
changes only whether the bar renders, never any other behavior.
